title: Cadentic Mesocycle Engine API
description: The single contract for POST /v1/mesocycle-proposal (Epic 2 story 0). Request, response, the LLM's answer, and every enum are defined here once: the backend compiles these subschemas with Ajv at runtime, and the Android app's ContractSchemaTest asserts its Kotlin types still agree with them. Nothing in this file is hand-mirrored on either side.

Category.description: A trainable quality the athlete ranks in onboarding. Mirrors com.cadentic.app.domain.Category.

Lane.description: How much wear the athlete accepts. Mirrors com.cadentic.app.domain.Lane.

Rating.description: A self-assessed level. null (not this enum) means the athlete skipped the question — unknown, never average.

Strain.description: How hard a blocker is on the athlete. Mirrors com.cadentic.app.domain.Strain.

DayType.description: What a planned day is for. Pinned to PRD §5.1. Game and team-practice days are NOT in this enum: the GUI overlays those from the Blocker Calendar, and the model never authors them.

Intensity.description: Reuses the Strain vocabulary so the product speaks one intensity language. null on — and only on — a REST day.

PhaseType.description: The phase's role, which the UI switches on. Deload timing is expressed as a DELOAD phase; there is no separate deload field.

MesoRequestPayload.description: The request body: exactly what Epic 1's MesoRequestAssembler produces, sent verbatim. The request id travels in the X-Request-Id header, not here, so the body stays byte-identical to the assembled payload.

requestDate.description: The temporal anchor, injected by the assembler. The cycle is calendar-anchored and one-off blockers carry absolute dates.

maxWeeklyDays.description: Optional athlete ceiling (2026-08-30, owner decision): the most days per week that may carry effort of any kind — planned training AND commitments like games or team practice, counted as distinct days, a day carrying both counting once. null means the athlete set no cap. The coach prescribes frequency; this only caps it. Weeks whose commitments alone already exceed the cap are exempt — the athlete's own calendar never makes the cap infeasible, it only stops the plan adding occupied days beyond it.

selfAssessment.description: All four categories are always present as keys. A null value means unknown, not average.

blockerCalendar.description: Two kinds and only two. A league game is a one-off like any other; there is no fixture kind and no schedule import behind one. An empty calendar is valid.

timeRange.description: OPAQUE free text ("19:00–20:30"). Consumers — the model included — must not parse it.

name.description: Display text only — the UI switches on phaseType, never on this. It is rendered inside a timeline segment whose width is proportional to the phase's length, so a one-week phase gets a very narrow box: one or two short words. 14 is not a target, it is a ceiling.

intensity.description: null on a REST day and on no other day type — checked structurally, not just here.

days.description: All seven days, in Monday→Sunday order. A day the athlete does not train is REST, never an omitted entry.

PlanDraft.description: What the model must return, and the schema handed to the Agent SDK's json_schema output format. Deliberately absent: exercises of any kind (machine-enforced by DayType plus additionalProperties:false), and headline/coachNote — plan surfaces never render model free text (PRD §8), so those stay deterministically composed on the client. lane/focus/queued ARE required here so a contradiction with the request is detectable; the backend then stamps its own values over them regardless.

startDate.description: Must be a Monday. Every week in weeklyStructure runs Monday to Sunday, so the grid is only coherent off a Monday start.

GeneratedBy.description: Backend-stamped provenance. The app persists it so a plan can always be traced to the mode, model and prompt that produced it.

mode.description: max-plan-oauth = Mode A (Agent SDK on the owner's subscription); user-api-key = Mode B.

MesocyclePlan.description: The 200 response body, and — once the app adds updatedAt — the mesocycle-plan.json artifact. Everything the model authored, with schemaVersion, generatedBy, lane, focus and queued stamped by the backend.

startDate.description: Must be a Monday. Every week in weeklyStructure runs Monday to Sunday, so the grid is only coherent off a Monday start.

ErrorCode.description: The complete set the app may receive from the backend. backend-unreachable is deliberately absent: that one is minted client-side when the app cannot reach the backend at all, and never travels over the wire.

ErrorResponse.description: Every non-2xx response. Named, never a stack trace.

message.description: Safe to show or log. Never carries provider internals, tokens, or a stack trace.

retryAfterSeconds.description: Present on rate-limited when the provider told us how long to wait.

fields.description: Present on payload-invalid: the named field errors, in Epic 1 story 6's style.
